h1:
Bueng Kan Riverside Restaurants
Mekong Breeze, Laos Views
intro: Bueng Kan runs right along the Mekong for almost the whole province, and once evening hits, the breeze off the river turns cool and easy — look across and you can see Laos clearly. That's exactly when the riverside places start filling up. The headliner here is giant catfish (pla khang) and Mekong river fish: genuinely fresh and genuinely big. We picked spots that are open right now, with locations, prices, and opening hours so you can choose by meal and budget.

blocks.html: If you come to Bueng Kan and don't eat at least one meal by the river, you haven't really arrived. The charm of this province is the Mekong stretching alongside the town, so most places set their tables facing the water — you eat while fishing boats drift past and watch the lights on the Laos side flick on one by one after dark. The star of the meal is Mekong fish, especially pla khang (giant catfish): firm, sweet flesh that works a hundred ways, from tom yum and blanched-with-dipping-sauce to phat cha and larb.

blocks.text: Riverside spots locals actually go to

blocks.html: We've ordered these starting with the ones that are easy to find in town, then the ones you'll need to drive a bit out for. The prices listed are rough ranges per person or per dish, and they can shift depending on the size of the fish and the time of day.

items.name: Krua Sawoey
items.blurb: The riverside spot Bueng Kan locals call their regular. Tables face the water with a full view of the mountains on the Laos side. The strength here is the giant catfish, cooked plenty of ways — tom yum pla khang, blanched pla khang with dipping sauce, larb pla khang, stir-fried Mekong fish phat cha, and choo chee pla khang, all bold and properly seasoned Isan-style.
items.meta: Mi Chai Rd, Wisit, Mueang district · open 4:00 PM–11:00 PM daily
items.price: Tom yum giant catfish THB 180–220 · THB 200–350 per person

items.name: Riverside Restaurant & Bar Bungkan
items.blurb: For a chilled evening, this is the one. It sits right on the Mekong on Mi Chai Road, nicely decorated, with a folk-song music corner out front, an air-conditioned room, and a wine bar with imported beer and wine. The standouts are larb pla khang and grilled wagyu-style beef with jaew dipping sauce. Good for hanging out with friends over a beer, watching football by the river.
items.meta: 100 Moo 1, Mi Chai Rd, Mueang district · right on the Mekong

items.name: Kin Lom Chom Khong
items.blurb: Out in Pak Khat district, sitting right on a bend in the Mekong — the evening view is good enough that plenty of people come back for it. Easy parking. The signature is giant catfish, both tom yum and larb, plus fried featherback fish cakes and Mekong-fish larb worth a try. An easy stop if you're driving through Pak Khat.
items.meta: 72 Moo 5, Pak Khat, Pak Khat district · open 11:00 AM–8:00 PM daily

items.name: Lom Choey Pla Phao
items.blurb: Over by Ban Tha Khrai, next to Wat Tha Khrai — not right on the water, but you can still see the Mekong. The draw is big grilled fish with firm flesh, grilled fresh every day, and a sweet-sour dipping sauce that hits just right. There's also grilled red tilapia, mu yo salad, duck larb, cucumber salad, and rustic mieng pla daek. Friendly prices.
items.meta: Moo 5, Rim Khong Rd, Ban Tha Khrai, Mueang district

items.name: Ran Pla Khang (Kan Fish)
items.blurb: The name tells you straight up you're here for the fish. The highlight is soft-fleshed Mekong fish, done as both phat cha and fried with garlic — tasty, with tender flesh. Good for anyone who wants Mekong fish without gambling on whether it's fresh.
items.meta: Chan Sin Rd, Mueang district · tel 042-491-037

items.name: Maenam Bueng Kan Restaurant
items.blurb: In the Wisit area, with a Mekong view from the restaurant. It's open from morning straight through to evening, which suits anyone wanting giant catfish outside the dinner rush. It uses the fish in plenty of dishes and makes a solid backup when the evening-only spots aren't open yet.
items.meta: 107 Moo 1, Wisit, Mueang district · open 9:00 AM–9:30 PM daily

blocks.title: Tip on timing
blocks.html: Riverside spots are at their best around 4:00–6:30 PM, when the breeze cools off and you catch the sun setting behind Laos. If you want a table right against the river railing at popular places like Krua Sawoey or Riverside, go before 5:00 PM or call ahead to book. Saturdays and Sundays are busier than weekdays.

blocks.text: Mekong fish dishes you have to order

blocks.html: Giant catfish is Bueng Kan's star — firm, rich, and free of any muddy smell when it's fresh. It's mostly sold by the kilo based on the size of the fish, and you can have the kitchen weigh it before you commit. These are the orders that rarely miss.

items: Tom yum giant catfish — bold, sour-and-spicy broth, properly seasoned, with firm fish. A dish that lands on nearly every table.
Blanched giant catfish with dipping sauce — just cooked through, dipped in seafood sauce or jaew, with the full flavor of the fish. Good if you want it without heavy seasoning.
Mekong fish phat cha / drunken stir-fry — hot and spicy with a light peppery note and holy basil, made for hot steamed rice.
Larb pla khang — Isan-style larb with fragrant toasted rice tossed through the fish, eaten with fresh vegetables and sticky rice.
Grilled fish / grilled red tilapia — grilled whole, tender flesh, dipped in sweet-sour sauce. A staple at the grilled-fish places.

blocks.text: Isan dishes to round out a riverside meal

blocks.html: Fish alone isn't enough — Bueng Kan's riverside places serve a full spread of Isan food. Order a few to share so you get a wider range of flavors.

items.name: Som tum + grilled chicken
items.blurb: The classic Isan-table pairing — crab-and-pla-ra papaya salad with a kick, eaten with grilled chicken and sticky rice.

items.name: Larb / koi, beef or pork
items.blurb: Larb with fragrant toasted rice, boldly seasoned — protein beyond the fish.

items.name: Mu yo salad / cucumber salad
items.blurb: A bright, sour dish to cut the richness — good to nibble while you wait on the fish.

items.name: Mieng pla daek
items.blurb: A truly local bite — wrapped greens dipped in fermented-fish sauce. If you like rustic flavors, give it a try.

items: Giant catfish is sold by the kilo, and a big one can climb into the several hundreds. If there are only a few of you, just ask the kitchen to pick a smaller fish.
Many evening spots open mid-to-late afternoon and run late (Krua Sawoey, for example, starts at 4:00 PM), so you may find them closed at midday. Check the hours before you set out.
In the dry season the Mekong drops and the view becomes wide sandbars, while in the rainy season the water fills the banks for a far more dramatic view. Each season has a different feel.
Plenty of places prefer cash; some take PromptPay. Carrying cash will save you the hassle.

faq.q: Which Bueng Kan riverside restaurant has the best view?
faq.a: Krua Sawoey and Riverside Restaurant & Bar on Mi Chai Road in town sit right on the Mekong with a full view across to Laos, while Kin Lom Chom Khong in Pak Khat district is right on a bend in the river with a lovely evening view. Pick based on whether you're staying in town or passing through Pak Khat.

faq.q: How much does Bueng Kan giant catfish cost?
faq.a: It's mostly priced by the size of the fish, by the kilo. A popular dish like tom yum giant catfish runs around THB 180–220, and you'll average roughly THB 200–350 per person if you make the fish your main dish. At a bar like Riverside, per-person spend can reach THB 500 once you add drinks.

faq.q: What time do Bueng Kan riverside restaurants open?
faq.a: Many evening spots open in the afternoon and run late — Krua Sawoey is open 4:00 PM–11:00 PM, Kin Lom Chom Khong runs 11:00 AM–8:00 PM, and Maenam Restaurant stays open long hours, 9:00 AM–9:30 PM. Check the times before you go, as some don't open at midday.

faq.q: What time of year is best for Bueng Kan's riverside restaurants?
faq.a: In the rainy season (June–October) the Mekong fills the banks for a dramatic view, while in the dry season the water drops to reveal wide sandbars — a completely different feel. Whatever the season, the coolest breeze and best light are around 4:00–6:30 PM, as the sun sets behind Laos.

faq.q: Is there a grilled-fish spot by the river in Bueng Kan?
faq.a: Yes — Lom Choey Pla Phao over by Ban Tha Khrai is the grilled-fish place people recommend. They grill fresh fish every day, with big firm-fleshed grilled red tilapia and a good sweet-sour dipping sauce, at around THB 101–250 per person.
